newsitem.title: EGYPT: Two Egypt militant groups unite and urge violence.
newsitem.headline: Two Egypt militant groups unite and urge violence.

text.p: Two Moslem militant groups in Egypt said on Monday that they have agreed to unify their ranks and that violence was the only answer to Israeli policies.
One analyst interpreted the statements by the Vanguards of Conquest and Jihad Movement to mean they could be planning to become more active.
"The need for unified ranks and groups waging holy war in Egypt has been agreed upon," their joint statement said.

Slamming Israeli occupation policy in south Lebanon and the building of settlements in Jerusalem, the statement said: "The only way to restore rights is the one of sacrifice, the same one taken by the Jordanian holy warrior..."
It was referring to the shooting last week by a Jordanian soldier who killed seven Israeli schoolgirls.

"We underline that there are many Islamic action groups in Egypt. All of them have one goal, which is waging a holy war for raising the word of Allah on earth," said the statement sent to an international news agency.

The two groups, which in the past have separately advocated violence to change the Egyptian government and replace it with a strict Islamic state, said that from now on they would issue joint statements.
Jihad was the organisation which assassinated Egyptian president Anwar Sadat in 1981. Police broke it up soon after, but some of its leaders fled the country and it remained loosely organised.
The Vanguards of Conquest emerged as an offshoot of Jihad, and in 1993 it tried to kill former prime minister Atef Sedki and Interior Minister Hassan al-Alfi.
Both are smaller than the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the main organisation fighting to overthrow the government and make Egypt a strict Islamic state.

"The two groups are not large now, but the merger could be a sign they are rebuilding the organisation," Hala Moustafa, an expert on Moslem militants at Al-Ahram Centre for Strategic Studies, told Reuters. "The move could mean they are preparing to carry out an operation soon."
In October, the Vanguards urged the army to use force to overthrow President Hosni Mubarak's government.

The government newspaper Al-Gomhuria said in September that Egyptian police arrested 16 members of Jihad's military wing, which planned to attack prominent figures and senior policemen, and to restore Jihad after the arrest of many of its leaders.
More than 1,000 people have been killed in Egypt since Moslem militants launched a bloody campaign in 1992 to overthrow Mubarak's government and set up a strict Islamic state.
